element_1_actor_rule_stop_clause.assessment: SATISFIED. read_only_character_check.verdict: The observation is genuinely read-only with respect to GitHub state. Constructing an unsaved draft in the configuration surface is a client-side act; no policy object is created, updated or evaluated. Ordering is also correct: D1 scope places this observation at index 1, explicitly 'before any recency mutation', ahead of ref creation at index 4.

sufficiency_without_overclaiming_post_sa.question_answered: Is a read-only availability/enabled observation enough for the required_change without falsely asserting that it demonstrates post-save behaviour?
sufficiency_without_overclaiming_post_sa.answer: YES for the required_change as written, which asks only for an observation 'recording whether the surface permits saving', not for a demonstration that a save succeeds. A read-only observation is the only construction that satisfies the finding without importing the very mutation the finding exists to gate.
sufficiency_without_overclaiming_post_sa.limit_that_must_not_be_overstated: An available/enabled save control is evidence about the client-side surface only. It does not establish that the server would accept and persist a zero-actor-rule workflow execution protection ruleset, nor what the post-save readback would contain. Nothing short of D2 can establish that.
sufficiency_without_overclaiming_post_sa.does_v4_overstate_it: NOT MATERIALLY, BUT IMPRECISELY. Neither artifact anywhere asserts that the D1 observation proves post-save behaviour, and GU-02's satisfied_only_if is scoped to visible availability. However the forbidden-claim strings 'actor_rules=[] representability proven before D1 observation' (spec V2) and 'actor_rules=[] representability assumed without the D1 observation' (design V4) are worded so that a careless reader could infer that the D1 observation itself proves representability. Recorded as B1N4-01, nonblocking.
sufficiency_without_overclaiming_post_sa.fail_closed_backstop_confirmed: field_by_field_D2_acceptance requires 'actor rule set empty' at post-mutation readback and terminates in 'any divergence => INVALID_EXPERIMENT'. The adversarial scenario 'actor-rule empty state appears representable but actual D2 readback differs' therefore resolves to INVALID_EXPERIMENT, not to a silent approximation and not to a false green.

B1S3_01_disposition.github_documentation_position: MARK_UNCERTAIN. Current official documentation states that workflow execution protections are built on the rulesets framework, come with two rule types (event and actor), and are configured by creating a ruleset and then adding event and actor rules. No official page reviewed states whether a ruleset can be saved carrying an event rule and zero actor rules. Documentary silence is recorded as uncertainty and is not converted into either a positive or a negative claim. V4's treatment of this as an empirical read-only D1 precondition is the correct handling of that silence.

The single-operator premise is therefore provable in principle on this platform, which makes V4's NOT_SATISFIED_AND_STOP a fail-closed response to an availability failure rather than a workaround for a documented gap.

B1N3_05_disposition.github_documentation_position: VERIFIED for the endpoint and capability facts. github_semantics_verified: Workflow execution protections are built on the GitHub rulesets framework and are available at the enterprise, organization and repository levels.
Actions policies are configured in a Policies section of GitHub Actions settings that is separate from General settings, and workflow execution protections are currently the only policy type.
Workflow execution protections define an allow list and come with two rule types, event and actor.

Event rules control which events are permitted, with push, pull_request, pull_request_target and workflow_dispatch given as examples, so pull_request_target is itself a controllable event and an allow list omitting it would remove the trusted liveness control. The spec permits it explicitly.
By default every user with write access to a repository can trigger workflows, which is exactly the residual that actor_rules=[] leaves in force and that the single-operator premise must carry.
Evaluate mode exists as a non-enforcing mode, which is why the spec's rejection of evaluate as a pass condition is a real distinction rather than a formality.
The documented configuration procedure is to create a ruleset and then add event and actor rules.
A repository collaborators listing is documented, whose permissions hash carries base role permissions and whose role_name is the highest role after considering all sources of grant.

A repository invitations listing is documented that returns all currently open invitations when authenticated as a user with admin rights, so the pending-invitation surface is observable in principle.
The repository contents create-or-update operation is documented as PUT on /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}.
OAuth app tokens and classic personal access tokens need the repo scope for that endpoint, and the workflow scope is additionally required to modify files in the .github/workflows directory.
The contents write request body documents an optional committer object, which is what makes the author/committer override prohibition load-bearing rather than decorative.
The current REST API version string is 2026-03-10, matching the value declared in rulesets_and_actions_prestate.api_version.
